### The Antibiotic Substance Entries Are Inconsistent {#sec-problem-details-30}

The surveillance end form records, for each systemic antibiotic substance the infant received, the substance and the number of days on which it was given, in up to nine substance entries.
An entry holds a substance together with its days.
A substance day is an antibiotic day and an antibiotic day is a patient day, so the days of one substance can exceed neither the total antibiotic days nor the patient days.
A substance is recorded in one entry only, since its days belong together.

Three messages report a violation of these rules: a substance recorded without its days or days recorded without a substance; a substance whose days exceed the total antibiotic days or the patient days, which includes a substance recorded on a form whose total antibiotic days are zero; and the same substance recorded in two entries.
The form shows the first entry once antibiotic days are entered and each further entry once the previous one holds a substance.
It asks for the substance of the first entry and for the days of every entry whose substance is chosen, and it insists on what it asks for only when the form is completed.
It does not ask for the substance of entries 2 to 9 when their days are entered, so days without a substance can be recorded on any form, and a substance without its days on a form that is not completed yet or that was written by a tool that does not apply these checks.
The other two shapes are not checked when the data is entered.

Please open the surveillance end form (see @sec-solution-15), reopen it for editing if it is completed (see @sec-solution-9) and complete, correct or clear the entries concerned.
When a substance appears twice, keep one entry with the correct days and clear the other.
